params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The small grey figure on the television screen stands blank and still for a beat, arms at its sides. Then bright green colour floods up through it from its feet to the top of its head in one quick rising wash, and the instant the green reaches its face an enormous grin splits open across its blank head, its arm snaps up beside its head with the fist closed and the thumb sticking straight up, and short radiating lines pop out around its head. It holds there beaming, thumb up, and gives the thumb one small extra push upward, then settles.

The figure stays inside the television screen as a picture on the screen in every frame, drawn in the same graphite line, and the word USER stays on its shirt in every frame. Its head stays a blank round head with a crosshair on it in every frame, with no eyes. The television, its shelf and brackets, the hanging cable, the shelf of binders at the left and the taped sketches at the right stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
